Quantified size of the value-preserving numeric-type ambiguity surface: 2^k=16 module digest classes for one nominal recipe, vs 1 under RFC-8785 JCS.
Bound on the fragility: structural (key-order/whitespace) re-encodings are invariant; only numeric TYPE is at issue.
Semantic characterization: the binding is nominal-exact, not tolerance-aware.

G1_injectivity_no_collision.note: On a designed lattice of nominally distinct recipes (amount, ingredient, sequence, tolerance, action, unit, step-count, list-order), both the module scheme and true JCS assign a unique digest to each -> the binding never UNDER-binds (no false-same collision). Complements the random tamper probes of packet-binding-parity-v1 with a structured injectivity lattice.
G1_injectivity_no_collision.source: HAC 1996 9.2.2 binding must be an injective map of the committed value

G2_type_orbit_module_fragments_jcs_colla.note: Every integer-valued numeric leaf (2 amounts + 2 sequence indices = k=4) may be legally spelled as JSON int or float by a conformant producer. Under the module scheme each independent spelling flips one digest bit, fragmenting the SAME nominal recipe into 2^k = 16 distinct formula_sha256 values. True RFC-8785 JCS normalizes all of them to 1. This is the quantified size of the ambiguity surface, extending canonicalization-conformance-v1's single-token int/float example (which flipped only `amount`) to the full numeric-leaf set.

G3_structural_invariance_both_schemes.note: Key-permutation and whitespace/indentation re-encodings leave BOTH the module scheme (sort_keys+separators) and true JCS digests invariant -> the residual fragility is bounded to numeric-TYPE alone; structural ambiguity is already prevented in the live scheme.

G4_binding_is_nominal_exact_not_toleranc.note: Changing amount 110.0 -> 110.25 g (inside the declared +/-0.5 g tolerance band) changes the digest under both schemes. The binding therefore commits the NOMINAL recipe point, not the tolerance-admissible set -- an intended-but-previously-unstated exactness property. A CRO measuring an in-spec 110.25 g must still reference the nominal packet; the digest is not a spec-band membership test.

G5_jcs_relock_unifies_orbit.note: Re-locking the Rust CanonicalHash to RFC-8785 JCS number rendering collapses the 16-way numeric-type ambiguity to a single canonical digest -- the concrete Phase-1 fix, consistent with canonicalization-conformance-v1's recommendation.

headline: An independent from-spec RFC-8785 JCS serializer characterizes the CRO formula binding as a two-sided robustness object: (i) it is INJECTIVE -- 12 nominally distinct recipes yield 12 distinct digests under both the module scheme and true JCS, so it never under-binds (no false-same collision); (ii) its ONLY value-preserving fragility is JSON numeric TYPE -- the k=4 integer-valued numeric leaves (2 amounts + 2 sequence indices) fragment the SAME nominal recipe into 2^4=16 distinct module digests, which true RFC-8785 JCS collapses to 1; (iii) key-order and whitespace re-encodings are invariant under both schemes; and (iv) an in-spec sub-tolerance perturbation still changes the digest, so the binding commits the nominal recipe point, not the tolerance band. The fragility is one-directional: the binding OVER-binds (fragile to benign re-encoding) but never UNDER-binds.
non_circularity: The oracle never invokes the Rust CroProtocolPackageV2 runtime; it re-derives every digest from the checked-in fixture bytes using CPython stdlib json/hashlib and a from-spec RFC-8785 JCS serializer. The module scheme is reproduced independently as compact sorted json.dumps and anchored to the shipped formula_sha256.
purpose: Quantify the invariance group and injectivity of the CRO formula binding -- properties neither packet-binding-parity-v1 (self-consistency + tamper detection) nor canonicalization-conformance-v1 (single-point byte-equality vs JCS) measured -- and size the numeric-type ambiguity surface (2^k) that an RFC-8785 re-lock removes.
theory_reference: Menezes/van Oorschot/Vanstone, Handbook of Applied Cryptography (1996), 9.2.2
